nav.title: IPEDS via NCES College Navigator - Sacramento State admissions considerations (fall 2024)

test_policy.notes: The CSU system no longer uses SAT/ACT in admission decisions; College Navigator (IPEDS fall 2024 admissions) lists SAT/ACT as 'Not considered (Test Blind)'. Sacramento State's international page lists no SAT/ACT requirement.

requirements.notes: Apply through Cal State Apply; $70 non-refundable fee by credit/debit card or PayPal. Needs a high school transcript with at least 3.0 on a 4.0 scale (or 80% average) and the diploma. Upload scanned PDFs through the International Admission Documents portal; unofficial transcripts and scores are fine at first. Passport copy required. Proof of funds is not needed for review but is strongly encouraged to avoid I-20 delays. Credential evaluations are not required (WES, ACEI or ECE only if submitted). College Navigator shows essays and recommendations are not considered.

deadlines.label: International application deadline, Cal State Apply (fall 2027)
deadlines.notes: Fall 2027 filing period is Oct 1, 2026 to May 15, 2027. Late-application appeals are accepted through June 15.

english_policy.waiver_notes: One option required. Sacramento State publishes a PDF list of countries where TOEFL/IELTS is waived (not read). MyBest TOEFL scores are not accepted; scores must come from the testing provider's portal. Also accepted: GTEC 1125, Sacramento State English Language Institute Level 7, ELS Level 112, FLS Level 16, TLC Level 9, UCLA Extension Level 6. Cambridge exams are not listed.

english.notes: Tests taken before Jan 21, 2026. ETS code 4671.
Tests on or after Jan 21, 2026; the page prints '3.5 IBT', which appears to be the 1-6 scale (verify with the university).

aid.notes: Sacramento State's scholarships page says the Scholarships Office awards nearly $4 million a year but does not say whether international students are eligible and names no awards. Contact scholarshipfaqs@csus.edu. No conditional-admission or ESL pathway is described on the pages checked, although its English Language Institute (Level 7) counts as English proof.

cost.notes: Computed from the Bursar page: tuition $3,419 per semester (6+ units) twice, campus fees $1,409 per semester twice, and the nonresident tuition fee of $471 per unit for an assumed 30 units ($14,130). Living on campus $20,212, books $1,240, transportation $1,528 plus personal $3,808 (other). The Bursar page has no F-1 budget; health insurance is not included.
